traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Loasaceae: leaves alternate or opposite; leaves simple or compound; compound leaves pinnate; veins pinnate or palmate; stipules present or absent; plants hermaphrodite; ovary half inferior or inferior; floral cup present; stems usually herbaceous, sometimes woody; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit usually capsule, sometimes achene or nut; stamens 5 to 100; carpels 1 to 5 (-7). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 385, 387, family Loasaceae: leaf incision lobed, often; read as {"lobed": "often"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 385, 387, family Loasaceae: inflorescence thyrse or solitary flowers; read as {"panicle": "often", "solitary": "often"}.
